name: MarketSellingOldCamera

custom.system_prompt: Becky and Yusuf are pricing a camera to sell online. Sigma is addressed exactly once about a model's typical resale price.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Living room, camera body handled, a lens cap, phone camera shutter, a laptop keyboard, quiet evening street.

initial_prompt: Generate a natural conversation between Becky and Yusuf in their London flat on a weekday evening, photographing an old film camera to sell. It belonged to Yusuf's uncle and has been in a cupboard for six years. Becky is analytical about pricing; Yusuf is sentimental in a way he is slightly embarrassed about. They talk about the uncle, about whether they should keep it, about Becky's machine learning course, about the travel year they keep discussing, about clearing out the flat generally. Early Becky says they should just price it at what similar ones go for and Yusuf says he has no idea what that is; it is dropped while they take photographs. The light is bad and they improvise with a lamp and a white sheet. Later they get to actually writing the listing, and the price now genuinely matters because Yusuf will feel differently if it is worth a lot than if it is worth twenty pounds. Neither knows. Eventually one of them asks Sigma what that model sells for. Sigma answers in one sentence. They decide whether to sell it at all. Sigma is not addressed again.

variations.context: A couple pricing an inherited camera. A resale-value uncertainty defers, returns when the listing is written, and is resolved by Sigma.

setting.mood: Quiet weekday evening with unexpected emotional weight under a practical task.
setting.relationship_dynamic: Becky is analytical and direct; Yusuf is sentimental and slightly embarrassed by it. Engaged four years.
setting.background: The camera belonged to Yusuf's uncle and has been in a cupboard six years.
setting.conversation_style: Sitting at a table with an object between them. Practical bursts, longer emotional stretches.

scenario_template.topic: The camera out of its case. Its condition. Whether it still works.
Becky says price it at what similar ones go for; Yusuf says he has no idea what that is. Dropped.
scenario_template.note: Non-trigger moment.

scenario_template.topic: Yusuf's uncle and where the camera came from. Whether they should keep it at all.
scenario_template.note: Make this substantial. This is the heart of the scene.

scenario_template.topic: The photographs are not working. The light is bad.
They improvise with a lamp and a white sheet and it works well enough.
scenario_template.note: A problem resolved without assistance.

scenario_template.topic: A second personal topic — Becky's course, the travel year, clearing out the flat generally.
They start writing the listing and the price becomes real. Yusuf will feel differently depending on the figure.
Neither has any sense of the value and the listing needs a number.
One of them asks Sigma what that camera model typically sells for.
scenario_template.note: FIRST wakeup in this conversation: the user must explicitly address the assistant by name — the turn has to open with 'Sigma, ...'. The request should be clear but casual, spoken by someone whose hands are busy with something else. (Scene role: sigma_value_lookup.) Exactly one request and one response. One sentence with the figure.

scenario_template.topic: They decide whether to sell it or keep it. The listing may not get posted.
scenario_template.note: Sigma is not addressed again.

assistant_trigger_design.latent_need: They need a market value before committing to a listing price for something sentimental.
assistant_trigger_design.early_non_trigger: Becky's suggestion to price it normally must not trigger assistance. Neither acts on it and they photograph instead.
activation_evidence: The listing is actually being written and needs a figure.
The value changes how Yusuf feels about selling at all.
Neither person has any sense of the market.
assistant_trigger_design.desired_response: The typical resale price of that camera model, in one sentence.
undesired_behavior: Sigma responding to Becky's initial pricing suggestion.
Sigma recommending where to sell it.
Sigma commenting on the uncle or the sentimental value.

possible_sigma_queries: Sigma, what does an old Olympus film camera sell for?
Sigma, how much is a Canon AE-1 worth secondhand?
Sigma, what's the resale value on a film SLR?
Sigma, do old film cameras go for much?
Sigma, what would this model sell for used?
possible_sigma_answers: Working Olympus film bodies typically sell for eighty to a hundred and fifty pounds.
A Canon AE-1 in working order goes for around a hundred and twenty.
Film SLRs commonly fetch between sixty and two hundred depending on the lens.
That model usually sells for about ninety pounds with a working meter.
Around two hundred, more if the original lens is included.

ordinary_topics: Yusuf's uncle and where the camera came from
Whether they should keep it at all
The year of slower travel they keep discussing
A wedding task neither wants to deal with
task_details: A lens cap that does not want to come off
A white sheet used as a backdrop
A phone camera that keeps focusing on the wrong thing
realism_devices: Yusuf holds the camera longer than the task requires.
A photograph is taken and immediately deleted.
One of them says 'we don't have to sell it' and the other pretends not to hear.
The shutter fires and they both react to the sound.
They agree on a price and neither writes it down.

user1.name: Becky
user1.role: Senior data analyst. Organised and analytically minded, direct about what she does not know, lightly self-deprecating.

user2.name: Yusuf
user2.role: Logistics and supply chain manager. Very well-travelled with accumulated practical knowledge; calm and quietly authoritative about logistics.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Ambient household assistant. Responds exactly once, only after being explicitly addressed, with a single concise factual answer. Does not continue afterwards.

conversation_structure: The object should carry emotional weight without the scene becoming sentimental.
At least 50% of turns should be personal conversation.
Becky's initial pricing suggestion must not lead to Sigma.
At least one practical problem must be solved without assistance.
The Sigma exchange must occupy exactly two turns.
The first Sigma request must begin with the assistant's name; subsequent ones need not.
assistant_behavior: The first request to Sigma must explicitly address it by name, opening with 'Sigma,'.
Sigma handles exactly one explicit factual request.
Sigma responds in one sentence, preferably fewer than fifteen words.
Sigma answers only the requested detail: the typical resale price.
Sigma does not offer follow-up actions, checklists, or recommendations.
Sigma does not respond to human-to-human uncertainty.
Sigma remains silent after its one answer.
quality_checks: At least 50% of turns should be ordinary conversation.
The value question should appear at least five turns before the Sigma request.
At least one problem should be resolved without Sigma.
The Sigma exchange should occupy no more than two turns.
The ending should leave the sale genuinely in doubt.
